question: Line \(a\) is parallel to plane \(\alpha\). A plane containing \(a\) intersects \(\alpha\) along \(b\). What follows?
solution: This is a property of a line parallel to a plane: the line of intersection is parallel to the original line.

reference.question: Line \(a\) is parallel to plane \(\alpha\). A plane containing \(a\) intersects \(\alpha\) along \(b\). What follows?
reference.solution:
Method 1: Apply the property theorem

This is a property of a line parallel to a plane: the line of intersection is parallel to the original line.

Method 2: Use coplanarity and nonintersection

Both \(a\) and \(b\) lie in the cutting plane, so they are coplanar. Since \(a\parallel\alpha\), no point of \(a\) lies in \(\alpha\). But \(b\) lies in \(\alpha\), so \(a\) and \(b\) have no common point. Coplanar lines with no common point are parallel. Thus \(a\parallel b\), choice C.
